newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey ready to give troops to Albania aid effort.
newsitem.headline: Turkey ready to give troops to Albania aid effort.

text.p: Turkey said on Monday it was ready to give troops to any international effort to distribute aid in Albania.

"We did indicate that Turkey is ready and willing to participate in any kind of military operation that will be designed to assist Albania," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news conference.
He said Turkey had sent an envoy to Albania carrying a letter to President Sali Berisha from Turkish President Suleyman Demirel.
Albania wants police units from abroad to help secure ports, airport, roads and railways so that relief supplies can be distributed.
An Italian air force Hercules transport plane landed at Tirana airport on Monday with six tonnes of emergency medical aid for the northern part of the country, which is under government control.

Neighbour Italy has already sent in some two tonnes of medical aid for the rebel-held south. Local committees run major towns in the region, though lawlessness is reported to be rife due to the activities of armed gangs.
Turkey signed a military cooperation agreement with Albania in 1995 and has held several joint military exercises with the Balkan country under NATO's Partnership for Peace programme.
